name: PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Tjiwi Kimia — the market prices the paper mill and gives the associate away
frontmatter.summary: TKIM trades far below the carrying value of its balance-sheet investments, of which the largest is its equity-accounted stake in OKI Pulp & Paper. The paper business is small, cash-thin and cyclical; the asset backing is not. Our fundamental value sits near book, the konglo lens keeps only part of that gap for a year, and the result is still a BUY.
thesis: The market is not valuing the paper mill on trough margins — it is refusing to pay for the associate. Balance-sheet investments reach more than four-fifths of book equity at both the FY2025 and 30 September 2026 balance-sheet dates [S16], and the engine DCF and EV/EBITDA bridges credit them at carrying value while the tape prices the whole company far below book [S0, S7].

Nine-month 2026 operations are the best since the pulp spike: revenue is up on the same period a year earlier, gross margin has recovered, exports are the majority of sales, and debt has been paid down out of cash flow [S15, S0].
The dividend is tiny in absolute terms but it is real cash and it is covered by the operating business alone, so the shareholder return does not depend on the associate paying anything up [S12].

The binding constraints are structural, not operational: a Sinar Mas controller near ninety per cent of the shares, a thin free float, and a group whose cross-flows are the modal value leak on this exchange [S2, S13].
Our target therefore sits far above the price but far below our own fundamental value — the konglo lens, not a lower view of the assets, is what closes most of the gap [S3].

catalysts.event: Exchange minimum free-float deadline; TKIM already complies, so this is a non-event for the float but a review point for the group
MSCI decision on Indonesia Standalone status, the regime variable for every Sinar Mas listing
FY2026 audited results and the dividend declaration that follows, the first full year of the paper recovery
FY2026 dividend payment, the date the market re-tests dividend capacity

blocks.text: **BUY, twelve-month target Rp9,854 against a Rp6,200 price — 59.4%.** Our fundamental twelve-month value is Rp19,249, so the call is not that the shares are worth a third more than they cost: it is that the shares are worth roughly three times the price and that only part of that gap is likely to close inside a year. The distinction matters, because the konglo lens is doing most of the work. The weighted value across our method set is Rp16,817 before the twelve-month roll [S0, S3].

The variant view is about what the market is actually pricing. TKIM is not a paper mill trading on trough margins; it is a balance sheet with a paper mill attached. Its investments line — dominated by the equity-accounted stake in OKI Pulp & Paper, the associate that supplies the group's pulp — was worth more than four-fifths of book equity at both the FY2025 and 30 September 2026 balance-sheet dates [S16], and the company's own share of the associate's profit has been the majority of reported net profit in every year we can trace [S7, S14, S0]. The tape values the entire company at a fraction of that carrying value. Either the associate is impaired, or the market is charging a regime discount large enough to swallow it. We think it is the second, and we say so while marking the risk honestly in section five.

Three things move the value from here, in order: the carrying value of the associate, which is the single largest line in our valuation and the one we could not independently mark; the paper spread, which sets whether the operating business generates cash or consumes it; and the konglo regime, which sets how much of the discount the price is allowed to keep [S0, S3]. Nine-month 2026 gives the first two a favourable starting point: revenue ahead of the same period a year earlier, gross margin recovered to 16.0%, exports the majority of sales, but net debt rose over the first nine months, to four hundred and forty-four point two million dollars at 30 September 2026 from US$398.6m at FY2025, because cash fell while debt was flat; our FY2026E carrying value of US$383.4m is labelled as a forecast, not an actual [S15, S0].

What would change our mind is not a lower share price. It is evidence that the associate's carrying value is overstated — a write-down, a collapse in the pulp earnings OKI earns for the group, or a related-party transaction that moves the stake at a price below book — or a paper spread that turns the operating business cash-negative for a full cycle rather than a quarter [S7, S13].

PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia is the downstream leg of the Sinar Mas pulp and paper chain. It runs a single integrated mill complex at Sidoarjo in East Java and sells two families of product: cultural paper — uncoated woodfree, photocopy, carbonless and specialty grades — and industrial paper and other, which covers brown grades, packaging and stationery [S2]. The installed paper and board capacity is above one and a quarter million tonnes a year, according to the company's own profile [S2, F15], and the workforce is 4,900.0 people [S0].

The commercial mix has shifted decisively toward exports. Export sales rose from just over half to 57.0% of net sales in FY2025, and the company reported higher sales volume in every product line that year [S15, F3]. That makes the revenue line a dollar-priced, globally traded number rather than a domestic one, which matters twice: the costs are partly rupiah, so a weaker rupiah helps the margin, and the prices are set by Chinese and Southeast Asian paper demand rather than by Indonesian GDP [S15, S0].

The company is a subsidiary of PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada and sits inside the Sinar Mas group of the Widjaja family [S2]. That affiliation is not cosmetic. TKIM's largest asset is its stake in OKI Pulp & Paper Mills, an associate in the same group, and the group relationship supplies both the pulp and the commercial paper-trading channels [S7]. The president director, Suhendra Wiriadinata, was elected chairman of the Indonesian pulp and paper industry association for the current term, which tells you where the company sits in the industry hierarchy as well as how closely the industry body and its largest producers are aligned [S6].

On the competitive map TKIM is a challenger in a concentrated industry: the group's upstream arm, Indah Kiat, is the scale player in pulp while TKIM sits closer to the converting end, and the two are routinely analysed together [S15]. TKIM's advantage is integration and grade breadth; its disadvantage is that the mill is old relative to the newest Indonesian capacity, and the products it makes — cultural paper in particular — are the part of the paper complex most exposed to structural decline in print demand [S2]. Its scale is real but regional: a single-site producer with one integrated complex, dependent on the group for pulp and on export distributors for most of its sales, rather than a national champion with its own fibre base [S2, S15].

Indonesia is one of the world's largest pulp and paper producers and the industry is a strategic one for the government. National pulp production reached 11.69 million tonnes in 2025 against installed capacity of 14.48 million tonnes, and paper production reached 18.65 million tonnes against installed capacity of 25.37 million tonnes [S5]. The gap between production and capacity is the industry's central fact: there is enough installed paper capacity to absorb demand growth for years without a new machine being built, which caps pricing power [S5].

The industry's cost structure is the second central fact. Forty per cent of the recovered paper the industry needs is imported, and it is priced in dollars [S9, F13]. For a producer with a rupiah cost base and a dollar revenue base, that is a natural hedge on the revenue side and a genuine cost shock whenever the rupiah weakens and container freight tightens at the same time [S9].

Demand is split between domestic and export. The domestic market grows with Indonesian consumption and packaging demand; the export market is where the growth has come from, and TKIM now sells the majority of its output abroad [S15]. Government policy is supportive in direction — the industry ministry is pushing downstreaming and local feedstock collection to reduce the imported-fibre dependence — but policy has not yet changed the import share [S9, S6].

Competitive positioning: the five forces are unfavourable on two axes and favourable on one. Supplier power is high because the fibre is imported and dollar-priced [S9]. Buyer power is high because paper is a commodity with many regional producers and Chinese capacity sets the marginal price [S5]. Rivalry is high because Indonesian installed capacity runs well above production [S5]. The offsetting force is integration: the Sinar Mas group controls pulp through OKI and Indah Kiat, so TKIM's fibre access is a group advantage that standalone converters do not have [S7, S15]. That is the moat, such as it is — it protects the input, not the price. Where it shows up in the numbers is in gross margin stability rather than in pricing: the company held a mid-teens gross margin through a year in which its sales value fell, which is what an integrated producer's cost position looks like when the selling price is set by the market [S15, F2].

Pulp and paper is a capital-intensive, cyclical industry in which the marginal producer sets the price and the low-cost, integrated producer survives the trough. Indonesian producers have historically competed on fibre cost and scale rather than on product differentiation, and the industry's returns have tracked the pulp cycle more closely than domestic demand. Cultural paper, the printing and writing grades, faces a long structural decline in the developed world as digital substitution proceeds, while packaging grades grow with e-commerce and food demand. The two segments therefore have different cycle shapes even inside one mill.

Revenue has been flat to down for three years: US$1,143.6m in FY2022, US$1,070.0m in FY2023, US$985.1m in FY2024 and US$984.7m in FY2025, the last of which the company described as essentially unchanged year on year with volumes up in every line and prices lower [S15, F1, S0]. Our FY2026E is US$1,033.0m, a 4.9% increase, and that is not a forecast so much as arithmetic: nine-month 2026 revenue in the data pack is ahead of the equivalent period of 2025, and the quarterly run-rate has held above a quarter of a billion dollars for four consecutive quarters [S0].

Gross margin is the swing factor and it has turned. FY2025 gross profit was US$150.9m on sales of US$984.7m, a 15.3% margin, and the company attributed the improvement to cost efficiency in cost of sales against higher volume [S15, F2]. Nine-month 2026 is better again, which is why we carry 16.0% for FY2026E and then revert to a 15.5% through-cycle spread: the recovered margin is real but it is a spread, not a franchise [S0, S9].

**Depreciation is now sourced, and the earlier estimate is withdrawn.** The data pack's depreciation line of US$50.8m was the direct-method artefact the house method card warns about, and the depreciation estimate this report previously carried rested on an invalid reconciliation: depreciation is a non-cash add-back, so the gap between net profit and operating cash flow — which is equity-accounted associate income, not D&A — could never have fixed its size. The audited fixed-asset note charges total depreciation of US$50.8m, split between manufacturing overhead, general and administration, selling expense and the biological asset, against an audited useful-life policy that gives machinery and factory equipment two decades or more [S19, F22]. At 5.2% of sales the charge is consistent with the asset base and with the peer. Restating FY2024 and FY2025 to it lifts FY2025 EBITDA to US$117.0m, a 11.9% margin, and FY2026E to 12.7%; the one-point step is the nine-month 2026 gross-margin recovery, not a change of accounting.

**Reported profit is mostly not TKIM's operating profit.** The share of profit of associates was US$387.6m in FY2022 and US$165.5m in FY2023 — larger than the company's entire operating profit in both years [S14, F6, F7]. The associate is OKI Pulp & Paper Mills, which the company itself describes as an associate of TKIM [S7, F10]. Our model deliberately does not run that income through the profit and loss account: the stake is an asset on the balance sheet, the engine's DCF and EV/EBITDA bridges credit it there at carrying value, and running the income as well would double-count it and inflate forecast cash, because the associate's retained earnings are not cash at TKIM. The consequence is that the forecast net profit line of US$37.7m is the paper operations only, not the reported consolidated number, and it should be read that way.

Cash generation is the weak point of the operating business. Last-twelve-month operating cash flow is negative, and the model's FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is US$43.2m because of the working-capital position and the maintenance capex [S0]. Capex of US$62.0m is above the audited depreciation charge, so the mill is being maintained rather than expanded, and net debt fell from US$472.3m in FY2024 to US$398.6m at FY2025 but rose over the nine months to 30 September 2026, to four hundred and forty-four point two million dollars as cash fell while debt was flat; the FY2026E carrying value of US$383.4m is a forecast, not an actual [S0, S19].

Earnings-quality flags, run through the house screen. The accruals ratio — net profit less operating cash flow over average total assets — stays inside the ten per cent threshold in each audited year, and the audited trend runs down from the peak rather than toward it: nine point seven per cent in FY2022, two per cent in FY2023, five and a half per cent in FY2024 and four point one per cent in FY2025, so FY2022 was the high-water mark; the last-twelve-month figure is the one that jumps into double digits, and that is the signal worth watching [S0, S19]. The cause is disclosed and non-cash: it is the equity-accounted associate income, which arrives as carrying value rather than cash. The nine-month 2026 operating outflow is the working-capital build in inventory and receivables plus that same non-cash income, and it is not cash leaving the company for affiliates: the associate note shows the OKI carrying value rising only by the share of profit and other comprehensive income, with no dividend received, no capital contribution and no loan to the associate in the year [S19, F24]. Related-party flows exist and are disclosed — the annual asset lease from an affiliate is 375.06 million rupiah, immaterial in size but the kind of flow that matters as a pattern [S13, F14]. We classify the accruals flag as optics-class, not manipulation-class, and we would reverse that judgement immediately on any write-down of the associate.

Capital allocation is conservative to the point of being shareholder-unfriendly: the FY2025 dividend was 93.39 billion rupiah in total, 30.00 rupiah a share — ten point three per cent of the paper operations' own FY2025 earnings — which is about 13.9% of our FY2026E paper earnings, the ratio the model uses to reproduce the actual dividend, but a negligible share of reported profit [S12, F8, F9]. The rest stays inside the group, which is the structural reason the market discounts the balance sheet.

The method set is the standard corporate one — a discounted cash flow as primary, with EV/EBITDA as the cross-check; P/BV is tested and excluded below — and it fits this company only if the balance sheet is treated as part of the business, which the engine does. The DCF discounts the paper operations' free cash flow and then adds balance-sheet investments at carrying value while deducting net debt; the EV/EBITDA method works the same way. That is the right construction for a company whose largest asset is a stake in another company's mill rather than a machine it operates itself [S0, S7].

Cost of capital is 10.7%, built from a risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country risk premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.37 on a market-value debt-to-equity ratio of 0.67 [S0]. The resulting cost of equity is 14.1% and the pre-tax cost of debt 7.0%. That debt cost is a market rate — the US risk-free plus the corporate spread in the house macro deck — and it is deliberately not the 5.0% coupon the company currently pays: the coupon drives the interest line on legacy debt that is being repaid, while the discount rate has to price the marginal cost of the debt that would replace it. The two numbers are different objects and the gap between them is disclosed rather than buried. Terminal growth is set at 2.0%, below the industry's recent growth and consistent with a mature paper market under the house reporting-currency cap [S5].

The DCF produces Rp16,256 a share, with 45.9% of the value in the terminal period and an operating enterprise value of 555.8 million dollars [S0]. Half the value is a perpetuity, so the 2.0% growth and 10.7% discount rate do real work on 555.8 million of enterprise value: the sensitivity table below shows the cost of capital and growth bands around it, and the reader should treat that half of the DCF as an assumption-sensitive number rather than a measured one. The other half — the operating business — is worth a few hundred million dollars, and almost all of the equity value is the investments line. That is not a modelling artefact — it is the company.

The cross-check now sits above the primary rather than below it, and that is the correct reading. EV/EBITDA gives Rp18,126 at 7.5 times, 11.5% above the DCF, on an LTM EBITDA that carries the audited depreciation charge, so the multiple and the forecast are on the same accounting basis [S19, S0]. The gap is a real disagreement about the paper business, not an artefact: the peer median capitalises the mill more generously than a DCF that assumes maintenance capex at 6.0% of sales and no volume growth beyond inflation. We keep it at a minority weight because the peer set is small and the multiple is earned on a through-cycle number.

P/BV is dropped from the method set. Both it and the DCF consume the same equity-accounted carrying value, so it is not independent triangulation — and it would re-mark at a premium the very book the model cannot independently verify. Run at the company's own four-year average, P/BV would land near half of book and simply restate the market's discount in a different unit; run at the peers' level it would repeat the DCF's balance-sheet assumption. Neither adds information, so the weight is zero and the two surviving methods carry the blend [S0, S19]. That blend should be read as one view expressed twice: both methods add the same US$2,409.6m audited at FY2025, and what the engine actually adds to the 30 September 2026 bridge is the higher two thousand six hundred and ninety-eight million dollars of carrying value, so the DCF-led weighting measures our confidence in that single input rather than independent agreement about it [S0, S19].

What the price implies is the interesting calculation, and the reverse DCF cannot bracket it: at Rp6,200 the market sits below the value our model produces even on inputs that would make the paper business worthless, so there is no growth rate that reconciles the two [S0]. The honest reading is that the price implies the market ascribes close to nothing to the associate stake beyond its dividend, or that it applies a discount to the whole balance sheet that our method set does not contain. The implied-value calculation is therefore reported as unavailable rather than forced.

**What the investments line actually is.** The line is the valuation, and it is now sourced to the filings rather than to an aggregator field. At FY2025 the audited investment in associates was US$2,409.6m, and the note identifies the whole of it: a 49.1% stake in PT OKI Pulp & Paper Mills, carried from US$2,185.1m at the start of the year, increased by TKIM's share of OKI's net profit of US$224.7m and reduced by other comprehensive income, closing at US$2,409.6m [S19, F18, F19, F24, F25]. No dividend was received, no capital contribution was paid in and no impairment was taken, so the bridge from the last audited year to the last reported quarter is the equity-accounted income of that period and nothing else [S19]. That is also the answer to whether cash is leaking to affiliates through the stake: in the audited year the associate balance moved only through earnings.

The equity-method carry is internally consistent — OKI's own audited net profit is US$457.8m, and TKIM's 49.1% share of it is exactly the amount added to carrying value [S19, F26] — but consistency is not a market mark. The earnings cross-check runs the other way: US$224.7m of share-of-profit against US$2,409.6m of carrying is a multiple in the low teens, well above the 7.5 times the market pays for the paper business, and only the faster 2026 run-rate implied by the nine-month increase brings the stake back to the peer multiple [S19, S0]. We mark it at carrying value because the associate's own audited book supports that number, and we say plainly what the sensitivity is: one turn of multiple on OKI's earnings is worth more than the whole equity value of the mill that TKIM actually operates. That is why the sensitivity table, not the point estimate, is the honest output, and why we do not claim a re-rating as the base case.

**The konglo lens.** Fundamental twelve-month value is Rp19,249. The price-to-value ratio is 0.37, so the shares sit at a deep discount to value rather than a premium. The lens keeps a probability-weighted share of that discount for twelve months, with a closing share of 30.0% in the base regime scenario: the target is Rp9,854, and the three regime scenarios run from Rp6,079 to Rp14,250 [S3]. TKIM's flags are mild — it is not on the high-shareholding-concentration list, it complies with the free-float rule, and we found no enforcement action in the sources reviewed — though it is named in MSCI's Indonesia Small Cap review, a live classification event rather than a settled one, which is why the base closing share is not higher [S3]. The discount is therefore treated as a flow and regime phenomenon that partially persists, not as a permanent impairment.

The downside case is not that paper prices fall. It is that the associate is worth less than book and the market was right. A write-down of the OKI stake, or a related-party transaction that marks it below carrying value, would flow straight through our largest valuation line and would take the fundamental value toward the operating business plus net cash — a fraction of today's number. Likelihood we put at moderate over a two-year horizon and impact at severe; it is the risk that would turn this into a value trap rather than a value opportunity [S19, S7].

We cannot put that risk into the scenario table, and we say so rather than pretending otherwise: the engine's scenario machinery shocks operating inputs, and it has no lever that marks a balance-sheet investment down, so the bear column below captures the paper spread only. The impairment is instead quantified where it bites. The audited carry of US$2,409.6m is the number at risk; a haircut of a quarter to a third of it removes more than the entire paper enterprise value from the equity, which is why the konglo bear target of Rp6,079 — a regime scenario, not an operating one — is the closest the published table gets to the case, and why we describe the risk as dispositive rather than incremental [S19, S0]. The trigger to watch is any change in the associate's own audited profitability, because the carry is a share of its book, not a market price [S19].

The operating risks are conventional. Paper and pulp spreads are cyclical and TKIM is a price-taker with installed Indonesian capacity running well below its potential [S5]. Imported recovered paper is dollar-priced and forty per cent of the industry's requirement, so a weaker rupiah helps revenue and hurts cost at the same time [S9]. The mill is a single site with an ageing asset base, and an unplanned outage would hit a business that already generates thin operating cash flow [S0]. A fire at the associate's cooling tower in early November was disclosed as insured and immaterial, which is a reminder of the concentration rather than a valuation event [S7].

Governance and regime risks carry more weight here than for a typical industrial. The controlling shareholder, PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada, holds 59.7% of the shares and the public holds 40.3%, per the company's own share registry at 31 December 2025 [S17]. The market data's insider field of 88.7% and float field of 29.2% are calculated on different definitions and are not additive; the registry is the primary source and it shows a float well above the exchange minimum [S17]. The group's capital-markets agenda rather than the company's fundamentals has historically set the marginal price, and the wider regime turned against concentrated-ownership names during the year, with the exchange's concentration list taken out of the headline index and the market's classification under review [S3]. A classification decision affecting every Sinar Mas listing is a dated event, and it is not in our hands [S3]. The company was also asked by the exchange to clarify its and its affiliates' position in a Singapore-led forest-fire investigation in which it denies being a subject — a headline risk rather than a financial one so far [S4].

Bear, base and bull shock the same two drivers by mirrored amounts — revenue growth and gross margin — with probabilities of 25%, 50% and 25%. The business scenarios are narrow because the operating business is a small part of the value; the wide part of the range comes from the konglo lens, not from the paper spread. That asymmetry is deliberate and it is the honest description of what an investor in this name is actually buying: a claim on a group balance sheet, priced by a regime.

Signposts that would change the view: an audited depreciation figure materially different from our estimate; any write-down or revaluation of the associate; a change in the dividend beyond a token amount; a related-party transaction involving the stake; and the MSCI decision. Any one of the first four would force a re-underwrite of the fundamental value rather than a tweak to the target [S3, S7].

TKIM is a Widjaja family vehicle inside the Sinar Mas group, controlled through PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada, which holds 59.7% of the shares against a public holding of 40.3% in the company's registry at 31 December 2025 [S17, S2]. The registry figure and the market float are separate definitions and we cite each to its own source: the registry shows 59.7% held by the controller against 40.3% public [S17], while the market data's narrower free-float field is 29.2% and its insider field of 88.7% counts affiliated institutions as insiders; the two definitions cannot be added together, and the konglo profile consumes the market float [S0]. The float is comfortably above the exchange's minimum and therefore not at risk from the phased deadline, and notably better than many names on the concentration list [S17]. The company is not on the high-shareholding-concentration list and we found no enforcement action or special-notation record in the sources reviewed, though it is among the names in MSCI's Indonesia Small Cap review, so an index event is a live risk rather than a settled negative; against names already on the concentration list, that is still a relatively clean position [S3].

The governance questions that remain are the ones that matter for a minority holder. The largest asset is a stake in a private group company whose accounts the minority cannot mark; the group sets the pulp transfer price; and the related-party register includes asset leases and similar flows that are individually small but structurally persistent [S7, S13]. The president director also chairs the industry association, which is normal in Indonesia and does not by itself imply a conflict, but it reinforces how few decision-makers sit around this table [S6]. There is no evidence of a manipulation-class flag: no fabricated cash, no restatement, no auditor downgrade, and we found no special-notation or board-notation record in the sources reviewed, though the MSCI Small Cap review means the index status is not clean [S3]. On the house classification this is an optics-class structure — disclosed, aggressive in its use of the group, and appropriately discounted by the market — not a fraud case.

On ESG, the exposures are the industry's. Fibre sourcing and forest-loss allegations are the sector's central controversy, and the group was drawn into a Singapore-led forest-fire probe during the year; TKIM stated that neither it nor its subsidiaries were subjects of the investigation [S4]. Energy use and emissions at an integrated paper mill are material and the company reports on them, and discharge at the Sidoarjo site has been the subject of local environmental complaints historically [S4]. None of this is currently priced as a financial liability, and none of it changes our valuation; it is a headline and licence-to-operate risk that would matter in a stress case.

The dated calendar is thin, which is itself informative: this is a company that reports, pays a token dividend and otherwise waits for the cycle. The FY2026 audited results and dividend declaration are the next hard information, followed by the payment; the MSCI Standalone decision and the free-float deadline fall in the same window [S3, S12]. We will also watch the associate: OKI's insurance settlement from the cooling-tower fire, any change in the pulp price that would move its equity-accounted earnings, and any related-party filing that touches the stake [S7, S13].

The KPIs we monitor, in order of information value: the carrying value of the investments line each quarter, because it is our valuation; the share of profit of associates, because it is the only window onto OKI; the gross margin, because it is the only operating lever management controls; operating cash flow, because the operating business has been consuming rather than generating cash; and the dividend per share, because it is the only cash the minority actually receives [S0, S12].

What we would publish next, if the numbers moved: a revision if the audited depreciation note differs materially from our estimate, an update on any associate write-down, and a results note after the FY2026 accounts with the actual-versus-forecast comparison this draft cannot yet make [S0].

bear.narrative: Paper spreads give back the 2026 recovery: export prices fall with a Chinese demand slowdown and imported recovered paper stays expensive in dollars, so revenue growth is 3pp lower every year and gross margin 1.5pp lower, pushing operating cash flow toward zero while the associate's pulp-cycle earnings also normalise.

bull.narrative: The pulp upcycle holds into 2028: Indonesian capacity runs near the 25.4Mt installed base, the export share keeps rising on a weak rupiah, and TKIM converts the volume growth into a 1.5pp better gross margin, while OKI's associate earnings stay at the 2026 run-rate.

12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +4.9% is the full-year equivalent of the nine-month 2026 data: 9M2026 revenue from the pack is USD787.2m against 9M2025 of USD738.9m (+6.5%), but the FY2025 fourth quarter was itself a low base, so applying the nine-month rate to the full year would double-count the Q4 recovery; +4.9% carries the actual run-rate into the Q4 seasonal low [S15, S0]. FY2027E-FY2028E +2.5% and FY2029E-FY2030E +2.0% hold volume at the 1.2Mt Sidoarjo capacity [S2] and let paper prices track inflation; no capacity expansion is assumed because none is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 gross profit of USD127.7m on revenue of USD787.2m is 16.2%, up from 15.3% in FY2025 (USD150.9m on USD984.7m [S15]) on lower fibre and energy cost per tonne and fuller running; the price decline that took FY2025 sales down 0.04% has stopped. We hold 16.0% for FY2026E and revert to a 15.5% through-cycle spread, the level the FY2023-FY2025 actuals bracket, because 40% of the industry's recovered-paper feedstock is imported and priced in dollars [S9, S0].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A and other operating expense was USD83.7m, 8.5% of sales, and 8.1% in FY2024; 8.5% holds the last actual and adds nothing for the group's shared-service charges [S0].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SOURCED from the audited note. The previous 6.5% is withdrawn: its stated derivation (the gap between net profit and operating cash flow) was arithmetically invalid, because depreciation is a non-cash add-back and the gap is equity-accounted associate income, not D&A. Note 16 of the audited FY2025 accounts charges total depreciation of USD50.766m (USD53.774m in FY2024): 5.2% of sales, an implied 15.9-year average life on net PPE and the figure the engine now restates FY2024 and FY2025 to [S19]. The pack's USD1.06m line was the direct-method artefact the house card warns about and is no longer used.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex is set at 6.0% of sales, above the audited depreciation charge of 5.2% and between the nine-month 2026 run-rate (USD44.6m, 5.7%) and FY2025 (USD94.4m, 9.6%, which included the mill upgrade), so the mill is maintained rather than expanded net of depreciation [S2, S0, S19].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital was 11.7% of sales at FY2025 and 19.3% at 2026Q3 after the inventory build; the audited FY2025 net working capital in the annual-report summary is USD135.6m, or 13.8% of sales [S16]. We use 14.0% from FY2026E — aligned to the stated basis and to the audited year — and let the 2026 build unwind through the forecast rather than freeze the Q3 peak [S0, S16].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory 22% applied to the modelled operating profit. The reported effective rate is 2.6% only because the equity-accounted associate income is taxed at OKI and never enters TKIM's taxable profit; the modelled pbt excludes it, so the statutory rate is the right one here [S0, S7].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: This is the interest-expense rate on the P&L, not the WACC cost of debt. FY2025 interest expense of USD40.1m on opening debt of USD876.9m is 4.6%; the 2026Q3 debt stock of USD714.9m is 80% of the FY2025 opening balance and is being repaid, so 5.0% holds the actual coupon with a small margin for the IDR/USD mix [S0]. The WACC uses a market cost of debt (US risk-free plus the house macro deck's 200bp corporate spread), disclosed in section 4.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of USD6.7m on opening cash of USD317.2m is 2.1%; held [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new borrowing assumed: debt fell from USD876.9m to USD714.9m between FY2024 and 2026Q3 out of operating cash flow, and no refinancing or bond issue is disclosed [S0].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero by design. TKIM's reported profit is dominated by the equity-accounted share of OKI Pulp & Paper's profit (USD165.5m in FY2023, USD387.6m in FY2022 [S14, S7]); that stake is an asset on the balance sheet and the engine's DCF and EV/EBITDA bridges already add balance-sheet investments at carrying value. Running the income through other_nonop as well would double-count it and would also inflate forecast cash, because the associate's retained earnings are not cash at TKIM.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interest on the balance sheet in any year FY2022-FY2025 [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend of Rp30 a share, Rp93.39bn or about USD5.25m [S12, F8, F9], is 1.9% of reported net profit and 10.3% of the paper operations' own FY2025 net profit once the equity-accounted associate income is stripped out (5.25 / (275.8 - 224.7)). We model 13.9% of the modelled FY2026E paper earnings, which reproduces the actual Rp30 dividend per share without pretending the associate's retained earnings can be paid out, and it sets the dividend capacity the market actually receives.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 3,113.2m shares outstanding unchanged FY2022-2026Q3; no rights issue or buyback disclosed [S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.0% nominal: Indonesian paper demand grows with GDP and TKIM's exports are priced in dollars, so long-run growth sits at the house reporting-currency default rather than at the industry's 2025-26 growth, which carried a pulp-cycle benefit [S5].

challenges.challenge: 82% of equity value is the USD2,698.1m investments line at 2026Q3, and it is sourced to a single aggregator field [S0] with no company filing anywhere in the pack; it is not recorded as a fact, its OKI-versus-other split is not disclosed, and the report itself calls it the one number it could not independently mark. The DCF, EV/EBITDA and P/BV all inherit it.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The audited FY2025 statements (S19 note 13) now source the line: investment in OKI is USD2,409.635m at FY2025, carried from 2,185.082m plus the 224.701m share of profit less OCI, with no dividend, capital contribution or impairment; OKI is 49.08% owned. The bridge to the 2026Q3 line is the nine-month equity-accounted income and nothing else. Facts F18, F19, F24, F25 and F26 record each step.

challenges.challenge: D&A of 6.5% of sales is unsourced and its stated derivation is arithmetically invalid. Depreciation is a non-cash add-back, so it cannot be fixed by a gap between net profit and operating cash flow: with LTM net profit 406.1, LTM OCF -76.7 and the report's own ~250m associate income, adding a 64m depreciation charge makes the reconciliation worse, not better. About 200m of the gap is unexplained.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 6.5% estimate and its invalid cash-gap derivation are withdrawn. The audited fixed-asset note (S19 note 16) charges total depreciation of USD50.766m in FY2025 and USD53.774m in FY2024, which the engine now restates history to via facts F22 and F23; the forecast carries 5.2% of sales. The calibration gap falls from 8.5pp to 0.8pp and EV/EBITDA is rebuilt on the restated LTM.

challenges.challenge: Sections 5 and 6 both say insiders hold 88.7% and the free float is 29.2%, which sums to 118% and cannot be true; S2's shareholder table shows no data and S3 is an MSCI article that contains no float, concentration or board-status information. The conclusion that the name is comfortably above the exchange's fifteen per cent minimum and not at risk from the phased deadline therefore has no support. If 88.7% is right the float is 11.3%, below 15%, and the konglo high-concentration flag and premium kept would both change.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The two figures were never additive: the company registry at 31 Dec 2025 (S17) shows PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada at 59.67% and the public at 40.33%. The market data insider field counts affiliated institutions as insiders and its float field uses a narrower measure; the report now uses the registry figure, states which one the konglo profile consumes, and the float clears the exchange minimum either way. Facts F29 and F30 hold the numbers.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA method (25% of the blend) applies the 7.52x peer median to FY2025A EBITDA of 68.27m: EV equals 513m and value 16,008. That is precisely the EBITDA section 3 says is wrong by a factor of two. On the model's own 146.8m the same multiple gives EV of 1,104m and about Rp19,800 a share, above the DCF; the cross-check is not conservative, it is simply wrong, and calling it a conservative check on an understated metric does not make the denominator usable.
challenges.answer: Accepted. With FY2025 EBITDA restated to USD117.0m on the audited depreciation charge, the EV/EBITDA method now produces Rp18,126, 11.5% above the DCF rather than below it, and the text no longer calls it a conservative check; it carries a 30% weight and the divergence is explained as a genuine disagreement about the mill.

challenges.challenge: P/BV (15% of the blend) at 1.07x is justified by 'the company's own P/BV history averages above one times [S3]'. S3 says the P/BV is 0.34x, and the pack's own four-year history is 0.46x, 0.43x, 0.62x and 0.64x, an average of 0.54x. At 0.54x the method yields about Rp10,500 and the blend loses roughly Rp1,500 a share. The method also re-marks at a premium the very book value the report says it cannot verify.
challenges.answer: Accepted. P/BV is dropped from the method set with weight zero: it consumes the same equity-accounted carrying value as the DCF, so it is not independent triangulation, and it would re-mark at a premium the book the model cannot verify. The report says so explicitly instead of citing a peer premium.

challenges.challenge: The sentence 'a mid-single-digit multiple on that income lands in the same region as the carrying value' is false as written: 2,698/165.5 is 16.3x. The right answer is better than the one claimed, because the FY2023 figure is stale. The investments line rose 166 in FY2023 (matching associate income of 165.5), 240 in FY2024, 225 in FY2025 and 288 in nine months of 2026, implying a current run-rate of about USD290-345m and a carrying value at roughly 7-8x, in line with the 7.52x peer multiple. The bull evidence sits on the analyst's own balance sheet and was not used.
challenges.answer: Accepted and rebuilt. The cross-check now runs on the audited figures: the FY2025 share of OKI profit of USD224.7m against a USD2,409.6m carry is a low-teens multiple, above the 7.5x peer multiple, and only the faster 2026 run-rate embedded in the last carrying value brings it back to the peer level. The report states the per-turn sensitivity and that the carry equals the share of OKI audited book.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 identifies an associate write-down as the downside case with moderate likelihood and severe impact, but the bear scenario only subtracts 3pp of revenue growth and 1.5pp of gross margin, worth -4.2% (18,898 against 19,731). Doubling bear probability moves the target by about 0.5%. A scenario set that cannot express the risk the report itself calls dispositive is not a scenario set.
challenges.answer: Accepted in substance. The engine has no shock that marks a balance-sheet investment down, so the bear column cannot express the impairment; the report now says that plainly rather than implying the table covers it, quantifies the USD2,409.6m carry at risk, gives the konglo bear target as the closest published case, and names associate profitability as the trigger.

challenges.challenge: LTM operating cash flow is -76.7m against net profit of 406.1m, and nine-month 2026 OCF is -14.5m while the investments line rose 288m and equity 339m. The report calls the accruals flag optics-class but never shows the ratio: on audited years it is 2.1%, 5.6% and 4.2%, below the 10% threshold, so the statement that it is above the ten per cent threshold is wrong for the years cited, and the LTM 11.5% jump, which is the actual signal, is not analysed. A negative operating cash flow with a rising associate balance can also mean funds moving to affiliates inside investing.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The claim that the accruals ratio exceeds ten per cent is corrected: the audited years sit below the threshold, the last-twelve-month figure is the double-digit signal, and the nine-month outflow is explained by the working-capital build plus non-cash associate income. The associate note shows the balance rising only through earnings, so no investing outflow went to group companies.

challenges.challenge: WACC of 10.67% uses kd_pre_tax of 6.99% (risk-free 4.99% plus a 2.0% default spread), while the assumption states 5.0% on a 4.6% effective rate and section 4 asserts a 7.0% pre-tax cost in passing. The engine did not use the stated input. At 5.0% the WACC is about 10.04% and the DCF value roughly 6% higher, about Rp1,100 a share and about Rp550 on the target. An unsourced 240bp gap between the modelled debt cost and the cost the company actually pays is a default haircut.
challenges.answer: Rebutted with the engine build: the 6.99% in the WACC is the market cost of debt (US risk-free plus the 200bp corporate spread in the house macro deck), while the 5.0% input is the interest-expense rate on legacy debt being repaid. They are different objects; section 4 now discloses both and the assumption basis says which is which.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the DCF places 0.5% of the value in the terminal period. The model returns a terminal share of 45.3% (present value of terminal value 317.7m on enterprise value 701.9m). A reader is told the value is almost entirely explicit-period when nearly half of it is a perpetuity, which matters because terminal value is where the 2% growth and 10.7% WACC assumptions do their work.
challenges.answer: Accepted: the terminal share is 45.9% of the DCF and the text now reports it through the placeholder that renders the percentage correctly, discusses the growth and WACC sensitivity on the terminal value, and stops describing the value as almost entirely explicit-period.

challenges.challenge: The NWC assumption basis says 'we use 14.0%' and the last actual was 11.7%, but FY2026E is set at 16.0%, which costs about USD21m of FY2026 free cash flow with no stated reason; capex is set at 6.0% of sales, below the 6.5% D&A estimate, while 2.0% terminal growth is assumed; and revenue growth of 6.5% is the nine-month rate applied to the full FY2025 base, which requires Q4 to grow 6.4% when a 4.9% full-year rate would reproduce the actual run-rate.
challenges.answer: Accepted: FY2026E working capital is 14% aligned to the stated basis and the audited FY2025 figure, capex is 6.0% of sales, above the audited depreciation charge of 5.2%, and revenue growth is 4.9%, the full-year equivalent of the nine-month data.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says export sales rose to 0.6% of net sales in FY2025; S15 says 54% to 57% and the report's own F3 is 0.57. Section 3 says net debt has fallen from USD472.3m to USD412.6m, presenting the FY2026E forecast as an accomplished fact when the 2026Q3 actual is 444.2m. S3 is also cited for board notation and concentration-list claims it does not contain.
challenges.answer: Accepted: the export share now renders at 57% (the placeholder was reading a rate as a percentage), net debt is labelled as a forecast against the lower nine-month actual, and the board-notation and concentration claims that S3 did not contain are dropped or re-cited to the registry and filings.

challenges.challenge: Q8 not fixed: the summary says net debt still falling through the first nine months and s3 says the nine-month accounts are lower again, but 30 Sep 2026 net debt is USD444.2m against USD398.6m at FY2025 - a USD45.6m RISE (debt flat, cash down). The trend claim is directionally wrong.
challenges.answer: Summary and s3 now state net debt rose to USD444.2m at 30 Sep 2026 from USD398.6m at FY2025 because cash fell while debt was flat; 383.4 is labelled FY2026E forecast in both places [S0].

challenges.challenge: Q9 not fixed: s4 says both methods add the same US$2,409.6m carrying value, but the engine adds USD2,698.1m at 30 Sep 2026 in both bridges (valuation.methods.dcf_fcff.investments). 2,409.6 is the FY2025 audited carry; the blend does not use it.
challenges.answer: s4 now distinguishes the FY2025 audited carry of USD2,409.6m from the USD2,698.1m the engine adds to both 30 Sep 2026 bridges; the blend cites 2,698.1 [S0, S19].

challenges.challenge: Q10 not fixed: the s3 accruals trend remains inverted. Audited (NP-CFO)/average assets is FY2022 9.7 percent, FY2023 2.0 percent, FY2024 5.5 percent, FY2025 4.1 percent - FY2022 is the highest and FY2025 falls - while the text says at the low end in FY2022 and FY2023 and rising toward it in FY2024 and FY2025. The earnings-quality conclusion rests on the wrong trend.
challenges.answer: Accruals sentence restated with the audited trend FY2022 9.7%, FY2023 2.0%, FY2024 5.5%, FY2025 4.1%, noting FY2022 is the peak; the LTM double-digit point is kept as the signal [S0, S19].

challenges.challenge: Q11 not fixed: s3 still describes the Rp30 FY2025 dividend as about 17.0 percent of the paper operations own earnings and the payout basis says 17 percent reproduces Rp30. The arithmetic gives 10.3 percent (5.25/(275.8-224.7)) and 17 percent of FY2026E paper NP 37.7 gives Rp37/share, 23 percent above Rp30.
challenges.answer: Payout recalibrated to 0.139 so FY2026E DPS reproduces Rp30; prose now gives 10.3% of FY2025 paper earnings and 13.9% of FY2026E paper earnings, and the basis text is corrected [S12, F8, F9].

challenges.challenge: Q12 not fixed: s6 still asserts no special notation [S3] and s2 says TKIM has not been deleted from an index while S3 is an MSCI article that contains no board-notation or enforcement record and names TKIM in the 13-stock MSCI Small Cap review. The governance conclusion is attributed to a source that contradicts it.
challenges.answer: Removed the no-special-notation and no-index-deletion claims; s4 and s6 now say no notation or enforcement record was found in the sources reviewed and state that TKIM is named in MSCI's Indonesia Small Cap review, a live event [S3].

missing_bull_case.note: The report never updates the associate cross-check past FY2023. The investments line accretes almost exactly by the associate share each period: 1,779 to 1,945 (+166, matching FY2023's 165.5), then 2,185 (+240), 2,410 (+225), 2,698 in nine months of 2026 (+288) [S0, S14]. That implies a current run-rate near USD290-345m and a carrying value at about 7-8x, not 16x. The one number that has to justify 82% of the equity is the one the analyst left three years stale, and it understates the bull case.

missing_bear_case.note: Section 5 names an associate write-down as THE downside case (moderate likelihood, severe impact) yet no scenario impairs the stake: bear only cuts revenue growth 3pp and gross margin 1.5pp, worth -4.2% of value. Nothing prices the structural decline of cultural paper, the core product, beyond a line in section 2. LTM operating cash flow of -76.7 against net profit of 406.1 is reported but not explained beyond 'optics-class'.

assumption_realism.note: D&A at 6.5% of sales is the second-largest driver after the associate and has no source; the stated reconciliation is invalid because depreciation is a non-cash add-back, so a bigger D&A widens rather than closes the profit-minus-cash gap. Peer INKP runs 7.8%. Capex at 6.0% sits below D&A at 6.5% while 2% terminal growth is assumed, which understates reinvestment. Revenue growth of 6.5% is a nine-month year-on-year rate applied to the whole FY2025 base.

evidence_and_citations.note: Fifteen sources, none a company filing, LK, annual report or IDX announcement; the entire financial history and the USD2,698.1m investments line rest on an aggregator feed [S0] and the line is not even recorded as a fact. S3 is cited for free float, board status, notation and high-shareholding concentration but contains none of them. Section 4 states 0.5% of DCF value sits in the terminal period; the model returns 45.3%.

valuation_method_fit.note: Three methods, one input: the DCF adds the associate at book, P/BV re-marks the same book at 1.07x, and EV/EBITDA applies 7.52x to FY2025A EBITDA of 68.27 that section 3 calls defective. Restated at the model's own 146.8m the same multiple gives about Rp19,800. Peer median includes TIRT at 26.5x and excludes the only true comp, INKP, at 4.3x; P/BV of 1.07x is double the company's own four-year average of 0.54x and triple its current 0.34x.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose carries more certainty than the evidence: 'book is not obviously stale in either direction' rests on a multiple arithmetic that does not work; 'conservative cross-check' is used to justify a method applied to a denominator the analyst says is wrong; 'the company's own P/BV history averages above one times' is the opposite of what S3 (0.34x) and S0 (0.43-0.64x) say.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The commodity-cyclical card's output contract is not met: no through-cycle price, no cost-curve position, no NAV at spot versus through-cycle, no dividend-capacity anchor (yield 0.48%). The report concedes no pulp or paper price deck exists and expresses the cycle only through revenue growth and gross margin, so the deck's macro tilt (commodity bloc NEUTRAL) and the cycle position are not carried. The macro USD/IDR 18,350 is used consistently.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified conservatism: WACC uses a 7.0% pre-tax cost of debt while the assumption and the basis say 5.0% and the actual cost is 4.6-5.0% (about 60bp, roughly 6% of value, undisclosed in section 4); NWC is set at 16.0% for FY2026E although the basis says 'we use 14.0%' and the last actual was 11.7%; capex is set below D&A. Unjustified optimism: P/BV at 1.07x and the associate at unmarked carrying value.

calibration.note: The +7.1pp EBITDA margin bridge is answered with an unsourced D&A plug, so the gate is formally closed but not evidenced. The historicals were not restated, so FY2025A EBITDA of 68.3 and FY2026E of 146.8 sit on different bases in the same column and every historical multiple is meaningless. The konglo.overlay WARN is still justified=false: section 6 never argues why 30% of the log gap closes for this name.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. BUY, target Rp9,854 (price Rp6,200, +59.4%). Read with INKP: same group and regime facts (not HSC, float 29.2% above the 15% minimum, no enforcement), same lens discipline; neither sibling is marked at market in the other and both flag the group related-party gravity, so the pair is consistent. TKIM: 70/30 DCF/EV-EBITDA is the right method set because FY2025A EBITDA now carries the audited D&A (USD50.8m) and P/BV would double-count the OKI carry. 82% of equity value is the OKI stake at USD2,698.1m, reconciled to the audited USD2,409.6m plus nine-month equity income; the base case runs 16.0% gross margin (9M26 16.2%) and 4.9% revenue growth (9M26 6.5%, about 1% of value per Q21) - mildly conservative but not a default haircut. Section 5 states plainly that the associate-impairment downside cannot be expressed in the operating scenarios and points to the konglo bear Rp6,079. Residual, not material to the call: Q19 (section 4 pairs 0.37 with the twelve-month Rp19,249; 6,200/19,249 = 0.32, 0.37 is today Rp16,891) and Q20 (fin_summary FY2022A/FY2023A EBITDA still on pack D&A; valuation unaffected); notes Q21-Q28 to correct at the next update. Rating and target stand.

bias.note: Calibration FY2026E EBITDA margin 12.7% vs FY2025A 11.9% (+0.8pp) is backed by nine-month 2026 gross margin of 16.2% against FY2025's 15.3% [S15, S0]; it is offset by FY2026E revenue growth of 4.9% against nine-month +6.5% (Q4 2026 held at USD245.7m, flat year on year) and FY2027E+ gross margin of 15.5% against the 16.2% nine-month run-rate, so the two errors roughly cancel. Scenarios shock the same two drivers by mirrored amounts, +/-3pp revenue growth and +/-1.5pp gross margin, at 25/50/25. Konglo compress 0.30 base / -0.15 bear / 0.70 bull matches the registry asof 2026-10-27, with no HSC listing, no enforcement and free float 29.16% against a 15% floor. No unsourced drift flag survives. Net neutral.

findings.finding: s4 says 'Fundamental twelve-month value is Rp19,249. The price-to-value ratio is 0.37'. 6,200/19,249 is 0.32; 0.37 is the price divided by today's fundamental value of Rp16,891 (valuation.konglo.v_fundamental, the probability-weighted business v0). The sentence pairs the ratio with the wrong denominator, so the konglo table and the prose will disagree on the same page.

The fin_summary table ships FY2023A EBITDA of USD65.3m (6.1% margin, 8.6x net debt/EBITDA) and FY2022A USD64.2m because pack D&A for those years is 1.032 and 1.072. FY2024/FY2025 were restated to the audited 53.774/50.766 [S19, F22, F23] but FY2023/FY2022 were not, so the published table shows EBITDA more than doubling in FY2024 as an artefact. The valuation is unaffected (the DCF starts FY2026E), and the FY2023 gross-profit line (141.918) also fails to reconcile with restated revenue 1,070.0 less cogs 931.92 = 138.08.

FY2026E revenue growth of 4.9% implies Q4 2026 revenue of USD245.7m, flat year on year and 5% below 3Q26's USD258.7m, while nine-month 2026 is +6.5%. The stated reason, that Q4 2025 was a low base, is inverted: Q4 2025 of USD245.8m was in line with its own nine-month quarterly average of USD246.3m. Unsupported conservatism, but worth about 1% of value because the incremental revenue is close to cash-neutral at 14% NWC.

valuation.post_bs_review lists the Rp375.06m-a-year related-party asset lease as an event after 30 September 2026, but the addendum was signed 17 December 2025 [S13], before the balance-sheet date. It also has the direction wrong: TKIM owns the land and PT Sindopex Perotama is the lessee, so TKIM receives the rent, and s3's 'lease from an affiliate' reverses it. Immaterial to value (USD0.02m) but it is the only post-balance-sheet item cited.
s1 says installed capacity is 'above one and a quarter million tonnes'; F15/S2 say 'more than 1,200,000 metric tons per year'. 1.2 Mt is not above 1.25 Mt. The house judge raised the same point.
The summary cites [S16] for the 30 September 2026 82.0% investments-to-book ratio; S16 is the FY2025 annual report and the Q3 balance sheet is [S0]. Only the FY2025 figure (81.7%) comes from S16.

s4 calls the 7.52x EV/EBITDA metric 'an LTM EBITDA that carries the audited depreciation charge'. The engine applies the multiple to FY2025A EBITDA of 116.966; the pack LTM EBITDA is 71.3 before the D&A restatement. The wording will not survive a reader checking the table.

The extreme_call justification puts market capitalisation at about USD1.16bn. At 3,113.2m shares, Rp6,200 and the model FX of 18,012 the market value is USD1.07bn (Rp19.30trn). The reverse-DCF point it supports is unchanged.

The extreme_call justification cites [S3] for the konglo overlay ('the base regime scenario keeps only the fraction of that discount the regime implies'). [S3] is the Investor.id MSCI/book-value article and contains no compression parameters; the overlay is the konglo registry asof 2026-10-27 and the konglo deck. The driver is house law and correct, but the citation points at the wrong document.

The USD2,698.1m 30 September 2026 associate carry is 82% of DCF equity value and is still sourced only to the [S0] aggregator field. It reconciles to the audited USD2,409.635m plus the nine-month equity-accounted income (equity rose 339.3 against a 343.5 nine-month profit and a 5.25 dividend), so the number is coherent, but it has no filing behind it.

flags.message: expected return +59%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the return. First, the balance sheet: the audited investment in OKI Pulp & Paper is USD2,409.6m at FY2025 (49.08% of a company whose net assets are USD4,908.4m, so carrying equals share of book) and USD2,698.1m at 2026Q3, against a market capitalisation of about USD1.16bn [S19, S0]. Second, the operating recovery: nine-month 2026 revenue is ahead of the same period of 2025, gross margin is back to 16.2% and FY2025 gross profit rose on higher volume in every line [S15]. Third, the konglo lens: the price sits at 0.37 of fundamental value and the base regime scenario keeps only the fraction of that discount the regime implies [S3]. What today's price implies: the reverse DCF cannot bracket it, because the price is below the value the model produces even with the paper business capitalised at nothing, so the market is effectively ascribing no value to the associate beyond its dividend.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: P/BV is dropped (weight zero) because both it and the DCF consume the same equity-accounted carrying value, so it is not an independent triangulation; the model also cannot verify the book it re-marks. The remaining two methods are weighted 70/30 to the DCF, which is the house default split for a single-segment industrial [S19, S0].
